origin_and_geography.native_tract: Thar desert of Western Rajasthan (Barmer, Jodhpur, and Jaisalmer districts), India, and contiguous Thar desert regions.
origin_and_geography.agro_climatic_zone: Arid desert and dry tropical scrubland.
origin_and_geography.historical_background: Name translates to 'that which crosses the Thar desert'. Developed by indigenous pastoralists to provide nutritious milk and vigorous draught under hyper-arid conditions where feed and water are scarce.

morphological_traits.horns: Medium length, lyre-shaped, curving outward, upward, and slightly forward with pointed tips.
morphological_traits.forehead: Broad, convex, slightly dished between eyes with prominent poll.
morphological_traits.coat_color: Striking white or light grey in summer; darkens to steel grey along the spine, neck, and hump in winter and during pregnancy.
morphological_traits.hump_and_dewlap: Moderately developed, firm hump; light to medium dewlap.
morphological_traits.body_conformation: Medium-sized, tight-skinned, muscular body; deep chest, clean strong legs, and resilient black hooves.

production_and_utility.primary_utility: Dual-purpose (valuable desert milk producer and active draught animal).
production_and_utility.draught_capacity: High endurance; capable of pulling ploughs in burning hot sand without fatigue.

management_and_resilience.diet_and_forage: Survives on poor-quality desert scrub, dry shrubs (Zizyphus, Acacia), and coarse desert hay.
management_and_resilience.disease_resistance: Virtually immune to heat stroke; highly resistant to tropical diseases and prolonged water deprivation.

conservation_status: Maintained at Central Cattle Breeding Farm (Suratgarh) and ICAR institutes; actively conserved under National Gokul Mission.
